1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Qingshi for three days straight. Lin Xiaoyu's sister had left for the capital in the spring, and since then, the little apothecary shop in town had been in her care alone.
After dark, she shut the doors and windows, counted the day's earnings, blew out the oil lamp, and went upstairs.
She had just lain down when an urgent knocking came from downstairs, followed by a man's voice: "Is anyone there?"
Outside the door stood a young man, soaked to the skin, his left arm wrapped in blood-stained strips of cloth. He said his name was Bai Yun, and that he was with the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need this wound dressed," Bai Yun said in a low voice. "I can pay — would thirty-five hundred wen be enough?"
He drew a letter wrapped in oilpaper from inside his robe. "This letter has to reach Qingfeng before the eighteenth of May."
As she bandaged him, he gave a wry smile. "If my fiancée ever found out I was knocking on a young woman's door in the middle of the night, she'd be eaten up with jealousy."
Lin Xiaoyu didn't take his money. She only said, "First thing tomorrow morning, I'll take you up the mountain."
2: They set out at first light. Lin Xiaoyu carried a bamboo basket on her back, packed with dried rations, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain, they met old Zhou Dashan, who was out chopping firewood. The old man put down his axe and lowered his voice: the evening before, three outsiders had been at the town entrance, asking about a wounded young man.
"Xiaoyu, you two should take the side path," Zhou Dashan said. "The main road isn't safe." Lin Xiaoyu thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Lin Xiaoyu walked in front, planting each step with care. Bai Yun followed behind her without a word.

At noon the rain stopped, and the mountain mist slowly drifted apart, revealing the rooftops of Qingfeng in the distance. A nun stood at the temple gate. Her name was Zhao Qiuyue, and she was the temple's guest prefect, in charge of receiving visitors.
Zhao Qiuyue took the letter, looked at the red seal on the envelope, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting 2 years for this letter."
Bai Yun said to Lin Xiaoyu, "I owe you my life." Lin Xiaoyu smiled. "Then next time you come, you can fix the roof of my medicine shop." Bai Yun stayed at the temple.
In the evening, Lin Xiaoyu went back down the mountain alone. By the time she got home, it was already dark. She lit the lamp and sat behind the counter for a long time.
